title: hotfix: SLO enforcer regional failover - threshold smoothing and backoff stabilization
author: Linh Nguyen
description:
Context: During a regional outage we observed the SLO enforcer oscillating between open/closed states and aggressively tripping regional circuit breakers. The immediate customer impact was a large number of 503s and an observed spike in tail latency for in-flight requests. This PR is an urgent hotfix to smooth threshold transitions, add stabilized backoff/decay on circuit-breaker reopen attempts, and add additional guardrails to avoid cascading regional failovers.

Summary of changes: implement exponential backoff with jitter for regional reopen attempts; add a configurable hysteresis window when transitioning enforcer state (OPEN -> HALF_OPEN -> CLOSED); smooth moving-average window used to compute error-rate and p95 latency for SLO checks to reduce sensitivity to short spikes; add a quorum check for multi-region decisions to avoid single noisy-region triggering global failover; add unit/integration tests and an emergency feature flag to disable automatic failover for affected customers.

Why this change: The enforcer was tuned for fast failover under persistent degradation, but during transient noisy conditions it could oscillate and provoke broader capacity thrashing. Smoothing and backoff preserve availability while still allowing genuine persistent issues to be isolated.

Risk and rollback: Low-medium risk; changes are limited to enforcer decision logic and are guarded by a runtime feature flag (slo_enforcer.backoff_stabilization). If regressions are observed the flag can be toggled to revert behavior without a code deploy. Rollback plan: flip flag to previous behavior and/or revert this PR.

Testing: added unit tests for backoff policy, hysteresis windows, and quorum logic; added an integration test that simulates transient spikes and verifies no global failover is triggered; ran perf canary in staging with 24h synthetic traffic, observed stable enforcer state and eliminated oscillation that previously occurred.

Related: references SUP-4237 incident timeline and ENG-8142 postmortem for root-cause analysis.
